control_implications.evidence_excerpt: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added a high-severity vulnerability impacting SonicWall SonicOS to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, following reports that it said may have been exploited in real-world attacks.
control_implications.headline: SonicWall SonicOS weakens authentication controls
control_implications.significance: The addition to the KEV catalog indicates active exploitation of an authentication bypass, which undermines confidence in MFA controls. Access management owners should verify that SonicWall SonicOS instances are patched and that privileged access reviews cover this exposure.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: Threat actors are attempting to exploit a recently disclosed security flaw impacting OpenSSH that can enable sign-ins to accounts that have no password set, according to Previdian.
control_implications.headline: OpenSSH exposes passwordless accounts to exploitation
control_implications.significance: Rapid exploitation of a vulnerability allowing sign-in without passwords indicates a critical gap in vulnerability remediation timelines. Vulnerability management owners should confirm that affected OpenSSH versions are identified and patched or mitigated.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: The login systems behind two car brands' mobile apps could be taken over completely, two security researchers found, allowing them to access any customer's account and, for an owner with a connected car, unlock the doors and start the engine. Both apps signed customers in through ForgeRock, an identity platform now part of Ping Identity
control_implications.headline: ForgeRock identity platform enables full account takeover
control_implications.significance: Default credentials on an identity platform allowed complete account takeover and vehicle control, demonstrating a failure in privileged access management. Access management owners should verify that default passwords are eliminated and that identity platform configurations enforce strong authentication.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: Some people who set up a Keplr crypto wallet with their Google or Apple account have had money stolen by an attacker. Keplr uses a company called Web3Auth to run that Google and Apple sign-in. The attacker used a security flaw at that company to reach the wallets, both companies said late last week.
control_implications.headline: Web3Auth flaw exposes crypto wallets to theft
control_implications.significance: A third-party authentication provider's vulnerability led to direct financial loss for users, highlighting supply chain risk in identity services. Third-party risk owners should review Web3Auth's security assurances and assess dependency on similar providers.

control_implications.evidence_excerpt: A single attacker using AI agents pulled emergency dispatch records covering seven Taipei districts, researchers at Acronis's Threat Research Unit said last week. The agents also found a Taipei fire department platform exposing patient data from 2018, including ECG readings and ambulance video footage, without a login.
control_implications.headline: AI agents extract sensitive emergency dispatch records
control_implications.significance: AI agents were used to access and exfiltrate highly sensitive health and emergency data without authentication, indicating a severe data protection failure. Data protection owners should confirm that emergency systems enforce access controls and monitor for automated data harvesting.

paragraphs.text: Active exploitation of authentication bypass vulnerabilities in widely deployed infrastructure — SonicWall SonicOS, OpenSSH, and the ForgeRock identity platform — and a third-party authentication provider (Web3Auth) demands immediate vulnerability and access management action. Control owners must prioritize patching, eliminate default credentials, and verify supplier assurances to prevent account takeover and unauthorized access.

AI agents are simultaneously automating core GRC tasks and being weaponized to harvest sensitive government and health data, requiring updated governance frameworks and stronger data protection controls. Risk and control owners should evaluate oversight of agent decision-making and ensure emergency systems enforce strict access controls and monitoring.
